To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

personality is an individual's unique, relatively stable pattern of thinking, feeling, and behaving, which is shaped by both heredity and environment, and that personality traits are relatively stable patterns of thinking, feeling and behaving.
the Big Five model is a useful tool for describing personality, but that the model is incomplete because it does not account for self-defining life experiences.
personality traits and self-defining life stories are 2 different ways of understanding the same phenomenon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the whole person and the whole person's place in a larger social and cultural world.
the person in his or her totality and with the person as an active agent of change in the social world.
the whole person, and we believe that personality theory and research should be too.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
personality psychology has not yet articulated a comprehensive and detailed statement of the whole person, but the current article is a step in that direction.

personality is a complex and dynamic organization of (a) behavioral, cognitive, and biological components, (b) different types of processes (including self-regulatory, self-reflective, and self-defining), (c) dynamic interactions among components within and between processes, and (d), the context and the environment, which is the source of the challenges, opportunities, and threats to which people respond.

personality psychology is the scientific study of the whole person, including the individual's unique variation from the common design for human nature and the self-constructed products of that variation, as well as the person's characteristic adaptations, all complexly and differentally situated in culture and social interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
personality psychology should strive to understand the whole person, not just a few aspects, and should seek to do so by articulating a framework that is at once both broad and deep.
the Big Five model is the foundation of personality psychology, but it is not the ceiling.
the Big Five model is a necessary but insufficient foundation for a science of personality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
personality psychology needs to develop a more comprehensive framework for understanding personality as a whole.
the time has come to move beyond the Big Five model to an integrative science that takes into account the whole person.
the Big Five is only a beginning.
